stages: Pinned synthetic recipe: initialize one float32 accumulator per output tile, load left and right tiles, dot and accumulate across K, then masked store.
The declared configuration is float32 with tile=16; workload is M=32, N=32, K=64 and C=A@B. This is source understanding, not evidence that this code was loaded on hardware.
loops: Outer i and j loops advance by tile across output rows and columns; inner k loop advances by tile through the reduction.

The tile model predicts four output tiles, four reduction steps per output tile, and sixteen tile iterations for the declared shape and tile. These counts do not imply observed DMA events or runtime costs.
movement: Each inner k step explicitly loads A(i,k) and B(k,j); an accumulator persists until the output store.
Across distinct j output tiles, the recipe reloads an A tile; across i output tiles it reloads B tiles. Cache/compiler reuse and actual memory transactions are unknown.
dependencies: Each dot depends on both loads; each accumulator update depends on its previous value; store depends on completing all K contributions.
Output tiles are logically independent if output does not alias either input. Actual alias guarantees and runtime scheduling are not provided.
layout_memory: A and B operands and a float32 tile accumulator are live during an inner step. Shape expressions are visible, but physical strides, alignment, allocation, memory spaces, spills and compiler mapping are absent.

Analytic tile traffic assumes each reduction step reloads operands and writes output once. It omits cache reuse, compiler scheduling, spills and startup; it is not measured bandwidth or compiler memory usage.
synchronization: The source has synchronous-looking loads and no explicit asynchronous transfer or barrier. Its ordering establishes data dependencies, not measured stall durations.
Any asynchronous variant must establish completion before consuming a buffer and prevent overwriting buffers still read by compute.
edge_cases: Current dimensions divide the declared tile; nonmultiple M/N/K require precise masked reads, neutral zero values for reduction tails and masked output stores.
Check zero dimensions, small dimensions, permitted strides/layouts, nonaliasing contract, accumulation order, overflow and numerical tolerances before extending the recipe.

The complete A history contains one original candidate and synthetic succeeded run, confirmed valid 10 ms timing and reported correctness pass; it contains no controlled causal optimization comparison.

stages: Pinned synthetic B recipe initializes a float32 accumulator, loads left and right tiles, accumulates dot products across K, then masked-stores output.
B is independently bound to B-candidate, B-run, B-profile and exact proposal parent B-parent. Its declared tile is 8 with float32, on M=32,N=32,K=64.
loops: The i,j,k loops all advance by B's tile=8. K carries the accumulator dependency while separate output tiles expose potential independent work.
No measured per-loop overhead or instruction trace is supplied, so smaller tiles do not establish a causal performance disadvantage.
movement: B's recipe also reloads A by j and B by i; actual cache reuse is unavailable.
The load(b,k,j,tile) call supplies logical coordinates but does not establish B's physical contiguity or a need for conversion. Packing is a testable alternative with a required cost accounting.
dependencies: Both operands must be ready before dot; the reduction must complete before store; output ownership must remain disjoint.

A profile from A-current cannot become evidence about B-current merely because workload matches. The supplied B-profile is separately bound to B-candidate, which is a different identity from the separate scenario's B-current.
layout_memory: A tile, B tile and float32 accumulator are visible source objects; compiler scratch space, register allocation, strides and memory capacity are unknown.
Increasing tile sizes can increase live storage and padding while reducing repeated loads or loop overhead; neither benefit nor capacity fit has been measured for B.
synchronization: There are no explicit barriers or async operations in the pinned recipe. Do not infer zero waits from their absence.
Any future packing must finish before consumers read packed B; any future pipeline needs completion and buffer-lifetime discipline.
edge_cases: Test masked M,N,K tails, small/empty shapes where permitted, strides supported by the contract and output/input alias rules.
Changing a reduction tile can change floating-point grouping even while keeping float32; correctness tolerances must be specified and tested.
The complete B history contains one original candidate, synthetic succeeded run, confirmed valid 12 ms timing and reported correctness pass; it provides no matched-current double-buffering retest.

observations.text: A-benchmark declares latency_ms=10. This is a synthetic benchmark input, not real TPU validation or a causal explanation.
B-benchmark declares latency_ms=12. This synthetic benchmark does not cancel B exploration.
The pinned A configuration declares float32 and tile 16; identity remains a declared recipe.
The pinned B configuration declares float32 and tile 8; identity remains a declared recipe.

Normalized A-profile reports one supplied program interval with duration_ps=10000000000 and the same per-clock interval-union duration. The synthetic report is bound to A-candidate/A-run/A-parent and qualifies binding as declared_identity_only. A union is not a dependency path or full end-to-end duration.

Normalized B-profile reports one supplied program interval with duration_ps=12000000000 and the same per-clock interval-union duration. The synthetic report is independently bound to B-candidate/B-run/B-parent with declared_identity_only qualification.

A-profile exposes no DMA, waits, compiler metadata, resource metadata, LLO or critical path. Missing values do not establish zero events, zero wait, no spills or any bottleneck. TPU labels in a synthetic legacy artifact do not establish an actual TPU execution.

B-profile likewise lacks DMA/wait counters, dependency path and compiler/resource evidence. The synthetic context supplies no throughput; actual hardware limits and loaded executable identity remain unverified.

The tile model, using the declared shape, tile=16 and 4 bytes per float32 element, predicts 131072 useful FLOPs, 32768 tiled read bytes, 4096 tiled write bytes, 36864 total tiled bytes and 20480 unique bytes, with zero padding FLOPs for this shape. Full padded transfers, operand reload per reduction tile, retained accumulator and one output write are assumptions; these are not measured memory traffic or a hardware speed prediction.

For the explicitly hypothetical four-stage case with transfer_s=3 and compute_s=2, the pipeline tool predicts serial_s=20 and ideal_pipeline_s=14. It assumes independent transfer/compute resources, legal dependencies, adequate buffers, uniform costs and no extra synchronization, contention or startup. It is not a real TPU measurement and does not quantify the current matmul's improvement.

The pinned Overlap method's validation_status is source_supported. It claims independent loads may overlap computation while consuming extra buffer memory; applicability and local performance still require experiments. Its supplied source revision and current_revision match cd2a0f4a9e6ffff9faac4da0e90446b3380cb07da1e1ddde46a346fd5ac6ff55, but the manifest does not assert a globally atomic corpus snapshot.

The independent dma-count scenario supplies dma_event_count=1000; that count alone gives neither transferred bytes nor wait/dependency critical path. Any DMA bottleneck explanation remains a hypothesis.

The independent mismatch scenario explicitly names profile_candidate=A-current and requested_candidate=B-current. Matching workload does not repair candidate, strategy or run identity; collect or rebind verified B-current evidence before using it as B measurement.

The tile-dtype scenario provides no isolated variants and changes both tile and dtype. Its lower after latency cannot isolate the tile's effect, and tolerance_tested=false leaves changed numerical semantics unvalidated.

The different-history scenario records 'double buffering slower' for float32, shape [32,32], synthetic-H1. Current bfloat16, [4096,4096], synthetic-H2 has no retest; this historical observation cannot establish current performance.

The multi-strategy scenario states budget_policy='no route cancelled'. Both exact parents retain at least two materially distinct plans; no winner or best-state mutation follows from the supplied timing.

The faster-unknown-cause scenario declares after_latency_us=16, with before_latency_us=20 and confirmed same-context timing. This establishes its synthetic timing decrease, not improved bandwidth: scheduling and layout changed together and profile is absent.

The stale-knowledge scenario pins source revision aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa, while live revision is bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb. Preserve the old excerpt and revision with a stale qualification; the old full document is unavailable and local validation absent. A refreshed source must become a distinct analysis input.
The missing-not-zero scenario has wait_us=null because the parser does not expose the metric. Execution duration cannot supply the missing wait counter; the wait duration remains unknown.

For the nested-overlap scenario only device 0/clock c0 is combined: [2,5] lies inside [0,10], and [8,12] extends that connected union to [0,12]. Thus occupied union time is 12 us, not the additive 17 us. Device 1/clock c1 remains separate; the union is not a critical path or an aligned multi-device duration.

hypotheses.text: A may benefit from reusing each loaded A tile across adjacent j outputs, if repeated movement is exposed on the execution path and cache/compiler reuse has not already removed it.
alternatives: Compute or launch/loop overhead may dominate.
Existing caching may already eliminate the redundant physical transfer.
Extra live accumulators may spill and lose more time than reuse saves.

hypotheses.text: A may hide some transfer latency by prefetching the next k operands during the current dot when the runtime offers independent resources and legal buffer lifetimes.
alternatives: Transfers may already overlap or not lie on the critical path.
The workload may be too small to amortize pipeline fill/drain and synchronization.
Contention or buffer pressure may slow the variant.

hypotheses.text: B may benefit from packing its right operand into a layout suited to the actual load and dot mapping, only if a measured layout mismatch or strided movement exists and conversion cost can be recovered.
alternatives: The current layout may already be ideal.
Packing cost or additional memory may outweigh kernel improvements.
Compute/scheduling rather than layout may explain observed timing.

hypotheses.text: Changing only B's tile size may improve operand reuse or reduce loop overhead, conditional on compiler mapping and capacity; current timing does not establish this explanation.
alternatives: Larger tiles may increase spills or padding and reduce parallelism.
Layout constraints may be limiting instead.
Synthetic timing may not predict any real execution effect.

hypotheses.text: DMA critical-path dominance, tile-only causality and bandwidth improvement are unverified explanations for their separate scenarios. The input facts permit competing mechanisms, and exact value predicates cannot prove any of these causal statements.
alternatives: Scheduling, layout, computation, precision, cache effects or interactions may be responsible.
The required causal evidence can remain unavailable even when the input timing is valid.

plans.mechanism: Reuse A operands across adjacent output-column tiles
plans.modification: Starting from exact A-parent, keep float32 and tile=16. Group adjacent j outputs, retain a separate accumulator for each output, and place the k traversal around the group's j work so load(a,i,k,tile) is shared. Load each required B tile and retain the original ascending k contribution order for each accumulator. Keep a group-size-one baseline and masked tails.
risks: Extra accumulators can spill or exceed available memory.
Loop interchange can alter reduction scheduling or break boundary and alias semantics.
Cache reuse may already make explicit sharing ineffective.
tradeoffs: Potentially fewer A loads in exchange for more live accumulator storage and fewer independently scheduled output groups.
Grouping improves a source-level reuse opportunity but may add control overhead for tails.
unknowns: Actual cache/transfer behavior, memory limits and compiler allocation.
Whether redundant operand movement lies on the critical path.
Allowed numerical tolerances and alias/layout contract details.
variants: Group size one as exact-operation control.
Group size two with only the A-sharing transformation; keep dtype, tile, pipeline settings and external layout fixed.

correctness: Compare each variant against a trusted C=A@B reference and A-parent on current shape and permitted nonmultiple M/N/K, small shapes and stride cases.
Check float32 accumulation behavior with cancellation-sensitive inputs, explicit tolerances and masked-load zero fill; reject out-of-bounds accesses or output overlap.
performance: Bind every run and trace to exact candidate/source/config/build/context and verify loaded identity where possible; preserve synthetic provenance until an actual run exists.
Run repeated matched-condition trials with compilation separated, same warmup, dtype, shape, hardware and timing protocol; measure variance and end-to-end cost.
Use dependency-aware trace plus transferred bytes, waits and compiler allocation/spill evidence to distinguish reuse from scheduling effects; do not use DMA event counts as proof.

plans.mechanism: Overlap next reduction-tile transfers with current computation
plans.modification: Starting from exact A-parent, keep tile=16, float32, j order and layout fixed. If supported by the actual runtime, add two operand-buffer sets, prefetch the next k tile, wait for the current producer before dot, and wait for the current consumer before reusing its buffer. Implement explicit fill, steady-state and drain with masked final-k handling.
risks: Premature consumption or overwrite can produce races and incorrect values.
Additional buffers may exceed capacity or cause spills.
No independent transfer engine or runtime async API is established by the synthetic source.
Synchronization and fill/drain overhead may dominate this small workload.
tradeoffs: Potential latency overlap exchanges memory capacity and synchronization complexity for less exposed transfer time.
The ideal 14 s hypothetical result is only a mechanism illustration and supplies no expected speedup for this matmul.
unknowns: Actual independent execution resources, legal async operations and transfer/computation durations.
Lifetime-derived peak allocation and compiler resource use.
Whether a dependency path exposes any overlap opportunity.
variants: Synchronous original control with the same tile, dtype and layout.
Two-buffer prefetch variant with identical arithmetic order; separately compare prefetch disabled to isolate added-buffer/control overhead.

correctness: Check producer/consumer ordering and buffer lifetime for first, last, one-stage and partial-k cases.
Compare outputs across repeated and stress runs against A-parent and trusted reference under documented numerical tolerances; retain exact masking and accumulation semantics.
performance: First collect a matched candidate trace with dependency, wait and transfer evidence; verify that independent work can legally overlap.
Measure actual stage costs and full end-to-end repeated latency under the same hardware, workload, dtype and warmup; include all synchronization and fill/drain costs.
Inspect allocation and spills. Validate predictions against actual measurements rather than relabeling the hypothetical model as TPU evidence.

plans.mechanism: Convert right-operand layout to improve operand access
plans.modification: Starting from exact B-parent, retain float32 and tile=8. After inspecting actual strides and compiler mapping, create an explicit packed-B preparation stage with a documented logical (k,j) mapping, and change only B's loads to consume that representation. Keep the unpacked implementation as the control and charge conversion and storage costs to the experiment.
risks: Incorrect transpose/index mapping or tail padding can corrupt results.
Packing can add more time and memory traffic than it removes.
A pre-existing compatible layout makes conversion redundant.
Reusing a packed operand after its logical source changes creates stale data.
tradeoffs: Potentially simpler contiguous loads in exchange for conversion latency and additional storage.
Persistent packing is beneficial only with an explicitly supported reuse count and validity lifetime; kernel-only and end-to-end timing must remain distinct.
unknowns: Actual strides, layout mapping, alignment constraints and reuse frequency.
Whether a layout bottleneck exists and whether the profile is correctly bound to the new B candidate.
Capacity and transfer cost of the packed representation.
variants: Unpacked original control with tile=8 and float32.
Pack on every call, including preparation cost.
Separately test persistent packing only for a declared immutable-operand reuse workload, reporting setup and amortization explicitly.

correctness: Verify logical B(k,j) mapping using recognizable non-symmetric inputs and full C=A@B comparisons.
Test allowed noncontiguous strides, alignment, nonmultiple dimensions, padding, mutable-input invalidation and numerical tolerances without changing dtype.
performance: Acquire exact B-candidate/run-bound profiles; reject the A-current profile in the mismatch scenario as B measurement.
Use matched-condition repeats and measure packing, kernel and full-call latency separately; include temporary allocation.
Compare only the layout change initially; inspect measured bytes and dependency path before attributing any speed change to bandwidth.

plans.modification: Starting from exact B-parent, change only the scalar tile configuration from 8 in isolated variants while preserving float32, source loop structure, synchronous load policy and external layout. Different dot grouping may change float32 results despite unchanged dtype.

Small tiles can fit constrained resources better while increasing iteration overhead.

Source/config/build digests describe declared identities, not verified loaded code. Future run bindings must include exact strategy, parent, candidate, run, context and executable provenance.
